title: Tobacco cessation tips and tools for your employees
summary: Help employees take the next step in tobacco cessation with proven tips, digital support, and health coaching options from Labcorp.
body_markdown:
November 19 marks the American Cancer Society’s annual[Great American Smoke Out](https://www.awarenessdays.com/awareness-days-calendar/the-great-american-smokeout/) , a nationwide movement held every November to raise awareness about the dangers of smoking, vaping, and chewing tobacco. If you or one of your employees uses tobacco, it’s the perfect opportunity to plan a healthy change.


Today, we’re focusing on actionable tips and tools to support the journey toward a smoke-free and vape-free life.


## Three tobacco cessation guidelines


**1. Commit to complete tobacco cessation**


Avoid dual use by not replacing cigarettes with vaping or vice versa. Engaging in both habits compounds your[health risks](https://www.cdc.gov/tobacco/e-cigarettes/quitting.html) and can make quitting more difficult.


**2. Set a quit date**


Choose a specific date to quit and give yourself a two-week window to prepare. Use this time to eliminate your supply, mentally prepare, and acquire nicotine replacement therapy or alternative substitutes.


**3. Tackle your specific triggers**


Smoking is usually tied to specific routines, such as drinking morning coffee, finishing a meal, or taking a work break.[Vaping](https://www.nhs.uk/better-health/quit-smoking/ready-to-quit-smoking/vaping-to-quit-smoking/how-to-quit-vaping/) , however, is often constant and borderless.


To quit successfully, plan alternative activities for structured outdoor breaks and develop a strategy to manage sudden, spontaneous indoor cravings.


## Remember the 4 D’s of tobacco cessation


The[4 D’s](https://health.usf.edu/media/xebnypbk/ahec-brochure-final.pdf) of tobacco cessation are highly effective for managing cravings from smoking, vaping, or chewing tobacco. Because intense urges typically subside within a few minutes, practicing these four techniques can help you successfully ride them out.


**1. Delay**


Wait 5-10 minutes before acting on an urge.


**2. Deep breathing**


Inhale slowly through your nose and exhale through your mouth to actively reduce stress hormones.


**3. Drink water**


Sip cold water slowly to stimulate your senses and interrupt the hand-to-mouth reflex.


**4. Distract yourself**


Change your physical environment or[shift your activity](https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/nicotine-dependence/in-depth/nicotine-craving/art-20045454) . Consider taking a walk or calling a friend to redirect your focus.


## Modify your environment


Eliminate all smoking-related supplies by disposing of all tobacco and nicotine products, including any hidden "emergency" stashes, to minimize the risk of a relapse.


Sanitize your environment by washing your clothing, bedding, and detailing the interior of your vehicle to remove lingering scents that can act as psychological triggers.


Establish[smoke-free boundaries](https://www.cdc.gov/tobacco/campaign/tips/quit-smoking/tips-for-quitting/index.html) by formally designating both your home and your car as strict "no-nicotine zones" to establish clear physical boundaries.


**H2: Behavioral substitutes**


Manage hand-to-mouth habits by keeping nicotine-free items, such as toothpicks, straws, or cinnamon sticks, close by to mimic the familiar physical gesture of holding a device.


Assess oral fixations. When you experience a sudden urge to reach for a tobacco product, occupy your mouth with healthier alternatives like sugar-free gum, hard mints, raw carrot sticks, or sunflower seeds.


## Access free digital tools and support


The QuitGuide app is available through[Smokefree.gov](https://smokefree.gov/tools-tips) . The[QuitGuide mobile app](https://smokefree.gov/tools-tips/quitstart) allows users to log daily cravings, identify behavioral patterns, and track overall health milestones in real time.


Text “Quit” to 47848 to join SmokefreeTXT. This service delivers 24/7 automated encouragement and practical advice customized to your specific needs and quitting timeline.
